findings.title: Device tagging is now synchronous on the anonymous auth hot path
findings.body: Previously TagDevice was invoked asynchronously in a goroutine with its own timeout/panic-recovery, decoupled from the request. Now `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, anonymous.AnonDeviceUI)` is called synchronously inside Authenticate, which runs on every anonymous request. This adds a DB round trip (CountDevices + Insert/Update) to the critical path of every anonymous page load/request, and removes the panic-recovery wrapper that previously protected the request from an unexpected panic inside the tagging logic. This is a meaningful latency/availability regression for a feature that is on the hot path for all anonymous traffic.

findings.title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic read-then-write, allowing the limit to be exceeded under concurrency
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices and then, based on that count, decides whether to INSERT a new device or fall back to UPDATE-only. There is no transaction or locking between the count and the subsequent insert, so multiple concurrent requests for different new devices can all observe a count below the limit and all proceed to insert, allowing the actual number of active devices to exceed deviceLimit. This undermines the guarantee the feature is supposed to provide.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new error-propagation behavior when the device limit is reached
findings.body: Authenticate now returns an error (failing anonymous authentication entirely) when TagDevice returns anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached, whereas other TagDevice errors are only logged. This is a behavior change with user-facing impact (anonymous users get denied once the device limit is hit), but no test in the shown diff (e.g. client_test.go) exercises this new code path to confirm Authenticate returns the expected error and identity is nil.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit default assignment yields an incorrectly narrow inferred type
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` has no explicit type annotation, so TypeScript infers the field's type as the literal `undefined`, not `number | undefined` as declared in the `GrafanaConfig` interface. Although assignable for the `implements` check, any code that accesses this property through the concrete `GrafanaBootConfig` type (e.g. the exported `config` singleton) will see the type as always `undefined`, even though at runtime it can hold a numeric device limit merged in from boot data. This can break type-safe usage of the field (e.g. numeric comparisons) and should instead be declared as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.

findings.title: New `device_limit` anonymous auth setting is undocumented
findings.body: A new `device_limit` key under `[auth.anonymous]` is introduced and read via `anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)`, but there is no corresponding update to the configuration documentation or sample/defaults ini shown in this change set. Operators have no way to discover this setting or its default/behavior without reading the Go source.

findings.title: 30-day expiration window constant is now duplicated across three packages
findings.body: The 30-day device expiration window is now independently defined three times: `thirtyDays` in impl.go, `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in anonstore/database.go, and `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in api/api.go. If one of these is changed in the future (e.g. to tune the retention window), the others can silently drift out of sync, causing inconsistent behavior between device counting, device listing, and device-limit enforcement.
